- [Software engineering practice briefs](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills.md): 305 authored practice prompts with expected evidence, hints, concept explanations and primary sources.
- [System Design Interview Questions](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design.md): Practice common system design interview questions with staged prompts, capacity math, failure drills, worked guides, and targeted concept review.
- [Design LLM Inference at 10K RPS | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/llm-inference-10k-rps.md): Work through requirements, token math, batching, GPU fleet sizing, reliability, and follow-ups for a 10,000 RPS LLM inference interview.
- [Design a Video Streaming Platform | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/video-streaming-platform.md): Design upload, transcoding, adaptive-bitrate packaging, CDN delivery, playback reliability, and cost controls for a YouTube or Netflix-style interview.
- [Design a Notification Service | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/notification-delivery-service.md): Design preference-aware push, email, SMS, and in-app notification fan-out with quotas, deduplication, retries, provider failure, and observability.
- [Design a Web Crawler | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/web-crawler.md): Design a polite distributed web crawler with URL normalization, robots enforcement, host scheduling, deduplication, recrawling, traps, and failure isolation.
- [Design Dropbox or Google Drive | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/cloud-file-storage.md): Design resumable chunked uploads, metadata, multi-device synchronization, versioning, conflict handling, sharing, durability, and storage cost.
- [Design Uber or Lyft | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/ride-sharing-platform.md): Design driver location ingestion, nearby matching, atomic trip assignment, dispatch, ETA, regional overload, safety, and marketplace observability.
- [Design Ticketmaster | Interview Guide](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/system-design/ticket-booking-platform.md): Design browse, virtual waiting room, seat holds, payment, oversell prevention, flash-crowd control, expiration, reconciliation, and fairness.
- [Engineering Learning Guides](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles.md): 7 long-form guides on evidence-backed software engineering learning: spaced repetition, Socratic assistance, artifacts, guest mode, and interview recovery.
- [Applying FSRS Spaced Repetition to Software Engineering Knowledge](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/applying-fsrs-spaced-repetition-to-software-engineering-knowledge.md): Explore how to use the FSRS algorithm for software engineering knowledge. Learn how an evidence-gated learning loop moves spaced repetition beyond rote memorization to systemic understanding.
- [Designing Useful Guest-Mode Technical Learning](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/designing-useful-guest-mode-technical-learning.md): Learn how to build a robust guest mode for technical learning platforms that persists complex state and transitions seamlessly to authenticated accounts.
- [How a Socratic coding assistant should respond to learners](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/how-a-socratic-coding-assistant-should-respond-to-learners.md): An AI shouldn't just hand out code. Learn why Socratic AI coding assistants must probe understanding, withhold direct solutions, and enforce the Feynman Gate to build actual mastery.
- [How to Turn a Failed Coding Interview Into a Learning Plan](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/how-to-turn-a-failed-coding-interview-into-a-learning-plan.md): Failed a coding interview? Don't panic. Learn how to extract signal from rejection, diagnose the root cause, and build an evidence-backed learning plan.
- [Recognition vs Causal Understanding in Technical Study](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/recognition-vs-causal-understanding-in-technical-study.md): Explore the gap between recognition memory and causal understanding in software engineering study, and how evidence-gated loops build durable mastery.
- [What Counts as Evidence of Mastery in Software Engineering?](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/what-counts-as-evidence-of-mastery-in-software-engineering.md): Explore why completed tutorials aren't enough and how to build verifiable evidence of engineering mastery through working artifacts, explain-backs, and tradeoff analysis.
- [Why technical learning needs an inspectable artifact](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/articles/why-technical-learning-needs-an-inspectable-artifact.md): Passive technical learning creates the illusion of competence. Discover why true engineering mastery requires inspectable artifacts, causal explanations, and rigorous evidence loops.
- [Build a search tokenizer](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-tokenizer.md): Write a tokenizer that lowercases, splits on non-alphanumerics, removes a small stop-word set, and applies simple suffix stemming. Use the exact same function for indexing and querying.
- [Build an inverted index](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-inverted-index.md): From a list of documents, build a term → sorted posting list map. Support a boolean AND query by intersecting posting lists. Track document frequency per term.
- [Calculate a TF-IDF score by hand](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/calculate-tfidf.md): Given term counts per document and document frequencies, compute the TF-IDF weight of a term in a document. Use dampened TF (1 + log tf) and IDF = log(N / df).
- [Calculate a BM25 score by hand](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/calculate-bm25-score.md): Given tf, df, N, document length, average document length, k1=1.2 and b=0.75, compute the BM25 score of a query term for a document.
- [Implement a BM25 ranker](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/implement-bm25-ranker.md): On top of your inverted index, implement BM25 scoring and return the top-k documents for a multi-term query.
- [Compute precision and recall by hand](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/compute-precision-recall.md): Given retrieved doc ids [1,4,2,9] and relevant ids {2,4,7}, compute precision@4 and recall@4.
- [Build a search eval harness](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-search-eval-harness.md): Create a labelled query set (query → relevant doc ids) and a harness that scores any retriever with recall@k, MRR, and nDCG.
- [Implement reciprocal rank fusion](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/implement-rrf.md): Given two ranked result lists (BM25 and vector), fuse them with RRF: score(d) = Σ 1/(k + rank_i(d)), k≈60.
- [Embed a corpus and search it](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/embed-and-search.md): Embed a small corpus with an embedding model, embed a query, and return the nearest documents by cosine similarity.
- [Implement similarity metrics](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/implement-similarity-metrics.md): Implement cosine similarity, dot product, and L2 distance. Show that on normalized vectors, cosine and dot product produce the same ranking.
- [Top-k with a bounded heap](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/implement-topk-heap.md): Given a stream of (id, score) pairs, return the top-k by score using a size-k min-heap — without sorting everything.
- [Build a brute-force vector index](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-brute-force-index.md): Build an index that stores vectors and answers top-k queries by scanning every vector. Benchmark latency as the vector count grows.
- [Explain HNSW search on paper](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/explain-hnsw-layers.md): Draw a 3-layer HNSW graph and trace a query: which layer it enters, how it greedily hops, when it descends, and where efSearch widens the search.
- [Add metadata filtering to vector search](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/implement-metadata-filter.md): Extend your brute-force index to support 'nearest WHERE field = value'. Implement both pre-filtering and post-filtering and compare results and timing.
- [Build a minimal RAG pipeline](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-rag-pipeline.md): Chunk a small document set, embed and index it, retrieve for a query, pack context, and generate a grounded answer.
- [Build a structure-aware chunker](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-chunker.md): Write a chunker that splits on document structure (headings/paragraphs) with a target size and overlap, instead of fixed character cuts.
- [Schema-constrained extraction](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/structured-extraction.md): Define a JSON schema and use structured-output mode to extract typed fields from unstructured text. Validate the result and reject on failure.
- [Build a tool-calling loop](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-tool-loop.md): Give an LLM two tools (e.g. search and calculator). Run a loop: model emits a tool call, you execute it, feed the result back, repeat until done.
- [Build an LLM eval](https://learn.significanthobbies.com/curriculum/drills/build-llm-eval.md): Create a dataset of inputs with expected behavior and a grader (deterministic or LLM-as-judge). Run it as one command and score a prompt.
